name: Handful of Stardust
summary: In the Ruins of Stardust, a pale frost gathers on the bushes south of Astranaar. Night elven healers use the powder to cool intense fevers.

sections.title: A Cooling Herbal Remedy
sections.body: Stardust clings to shrubs in the Ruins of Stardust, south of Astranaar. The fine powder shines like frost. Lingering elemental spirits haunt the ruins, yet plants thrive among the broken stones and take in a rare glow. Night elven healers make the residue into poultices for dangerous, persistent fevers. They turn to it when ordinary salves and moonwell waters bring no full relief.

sections.title: A Father's Hope
sections.body: Pelturas Whitemoon, a worried father in Astranaar, followed herbalist Orendil Broadleaf's advice and sought the powder. His young daughter, Relara, suffered from a stubborn magical ailment and nightmares. A blessing from a stone touched by Elune first calmed her mind, but her intense fever remained. Pelturas sought stardust to make a cooling paste and save her life.

faq.q: Where is the Handful of Stardust found?
faq.answer: You can gather stardust from the shining bushes in the Ruins of Stardust, south of Astranaar in central Ashenvale.

faq.q: What is this stardust used for?
faq.answer: Pelturas Whitemoon uses the powder in a soothing poultice for the unrelenting fever afflicting his daughter, Relara.

faq.q: What dangers surround the stardust bushes?
faq.answer: Hostile water elementals lurk near the shoreline and among the fallen pillars in the Ruins of Stardust, where the bushes grow.

faq.q: Is stardust related to the goddess Elune?
faq.answer: Night elves revere celestial powers, and the ruins bear a starry name, but herbalists recommend stardust for its frosted, cooling nature as a physical medicine.

angles.text: You gather stardust by hand from shining bushes. It reflects the night elves' use of rare local plants in restorative medicine.
As a Night Elf defending Ashenvale, you can see the bond between local remedies and your people's ancient ruins and herbal traditions.
